offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third); Class C Felony (fourth+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While in an intoxicated condition
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
enhancements: Chronic/habitual offender (5+ priors, Class B Felony)
notes: Missouri uses 'DWI' (Driving While Intoxicated). Prior offender status is lifetime lookback. Aggravated offender (BAC .15+) or chronic offender (5+ priors) have enhanced penalties. 30-day license suspension first offense.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while intoxicated or with BAC .08+
No prior DWI convictions
notes: 30-day license suspension followed by 60-day restricted driving privilege. SIS (Suspended Imposition of Sentence) available for first offense.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third); Class C Felony (fourth); Class B Felony (fifth+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while intoxicated or with BAC .08+
One or more prior DWI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 10 days or 240 hours community service (prior offender); 30 days (persistent offender); 60 days (chronic offender); 2 years (habitual offender)
enhancements: Persistent offender — 2+ priors (Class D Felony, 30-day mandatory)
Chronic offender — 4+ priors (Class C Felony, 60-day mandatory)
Habitual offender — 5+ priors (Class B Felony, 2-year mandatory)
notes: Missouri uses lifetime lookback. Each prior increases classification. Chronic and habitual offenders face mandatory minimum incarceration.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While in an intoxicated condition due to the influence of drugs or a combination of drugs and alcohol
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of drugs and alcohol
notes: No per se drug limit. Prosecution relies on officer observations, Drug Recognition Expert evaluations, and toxicology. Same penalties as alcohol DWI.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (general); Class A Misdemeanor (involving accident)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in a careless and imprudent manner
Involving an accident or endangering the life, limb, or property of another
notes: Missouri uses 'careless and imprudent driving' rather than 'reckless driving.' Common plea-down from DWI.

statute_title: Leaving Scene of Accident — Injury or Death
offense_class: Class D Felony (injury); Class B Felony (death)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury or death
Defendant failed to stop and remain at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render aid
notes: Hit-and-run causing death is a Class B Felony. Property damage only (§ 577.060(1)) is a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
While operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated
notes: DWI-related deaths are charged as involuntary manslaughter in Missouri. May also be charged as second-degree murder if extreme recklessness shown.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence while operating a motor vehicle
notes: Lower standard than first-degree involuntary manslaughter. Criminal negligence rather than recklessness.

offense_class: Class D Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent); Class D Felony (3+ or DWI-related)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was revoked or suspended
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the revocation or suspension
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Driving while revoked due to DWI is automatically a felony. Additional suspension upon conviction.

statute_title: Resisting Arrest by Fleeing — Motor Vehicle
offense_class: Class D Felony (creating substantial risk of injury/death)
elements: A law enforcement officer attempted to make a lawful stop or arrest
Defendant fled by means of a motor vehicle
Creating a substantial risk of serious physical injury or death
notes: Fleeing that creates substantial risk is a Class D Felony. Resisting by fleeing on foot (§ 575.150(1)) is a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony (most controlled substances)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Missouri Comprehensive Drug Control Act schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription
enhancements: Possession near a school, park, or public housing (§ 579.074)
notes: Simple possession of most controlled substances is a Class D Felony in Missouri. Drug courts and alternative sentencing available.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (personal use amounts); Class D Felony (over 3 oz without license)
penalty_max: 1 year (misdemeanor over 3 oz without license for those 21+); 7 years (Class D Felony large amounts)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Amount exceeded legal personal use limits for adults 21+
notes: Missouri legalized recreational marijuana in 2022 (Amendment 3). Adults 21+ may possess up to 3 oz. Possession over 3 oz without a license is a misdemeanor; larger amounts or distribution without license remain criminal.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance in Missouri
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Simple possession of cocaine is a Class D Felony. Larger quantities trigger distribution or trafficking charges.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine is a major enforcement priority in Missouri. Manufacturing carries separate enhanced penalties under § 579.055.

offense_class: Class B Felony (general); Class A Felony (large quantities)
penalty_max: 15 years (Class B); 30 years or Life (Class A)
elements: Defendant possessed, purchased, manufactured, or distributed
A quantity of controlled substance meeting trafficking thresholds
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (cannot be probated or paroled before 80%)
notes: First-degree trafficking thresholds: cocaine 150g, heroin 8g, methamphetamine 8g. Mandatory minimum served at 80%. Second-degree trafficking (§ 579.068) is a Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class C Felony (most); Class B Felony (to minor or near school)
elements: Defendant knowingly distributed, delivered, manufactured, or produced a controlled substance
enhancements: Distribution to a minor (Class B Felony)
Distribution near a school, park, or public housing (§ 579.074)
notes: Delivery is distinguished from trafficking by quantity. Near-school zone enhancement elevates by one class.

offense_class: Class B Felony (general); Class A Felony (meth with child present)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
notes: Missouri was historically a leading state for meth production. Manufacturing meth carries a mandatory 10-year minimum.

offense_class: Class D Misdemeanor (general); Class A Misdemeanor (delivery to minor)
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use for planting, propagating, testing, analyzing, packing, or consuming a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Low-level offense. Marijuana-related paraphernalia for personal use by adults 21+ is legal under Amendment 3.

offense_class: Class C Felony (most); Class B Felony (near school or to minor)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
With intent to distribute, deliver, or sell
notes: Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, and other indicators. Same penalties as actual distribution.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly caused the death of another person
After deliberation upon the matter
mandatory_minimum: Life without parole (if death penalty not imposed)
enhancements: Aggravating factors for death penalty consideration
Murder of a law enforcement officer
Murder during commission of certain felonies
notes: Missouri retains the death penalty. First-degree murder requires deliberation (premeditation). If death penalty not imposed, mandatory life without parole.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly caused the death of another person
Or knowingly caused or aided another to commit suicide
Without deliberation
notes: Second-degree murder is an intentional killing without deliberation, or a killing committed with extreme recklessness (depraved heart). 10-year minimum to life.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Under the influence of sudden passion arising from adequate provocation
notes: Heat of passion defense reduces murder to voluntary manslaughter. 5-year mandatory minimum.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
notes: First-degree involuntary manslaughter requires recklessness. Second-degree (§ 565.027) requires criminal negligence and is a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant attempted to kill or knowingly caused or attempted to cause serious physical injury to another person
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer (§ 565.082)
notes: First-degree assault is the most serious assault charge. Second-degree (§ 565.054) is a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class E Felony (general); Class D Felony (special victim)
elements: Defendant attempted to cause or recklessly caused physical injury to another person
Or with criminal negligence caused physical injury by means of a deadly weapon
Or placed another person in apprehension of immediate physical injury
enhancements: Special victim (law enforcement, elderly, disabled, etc.)
notes: Third-degree assault is the general simple assault charge. Fourth-degree (§ 565.058) is a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly caused or attempted to cause physical injury to another
By means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: Second-degree assault covers injury by means of a deadly weapon. First-degree is reserved for serious physical injury or attempt to kill.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant forcibly stole property
By use of physical force or threat of immediate use of physical force
notes: Second-degree robbery is unarmed robbery by force or threat. First-degree (§ 570.023) involves a dangerous instrument or weapon.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant forcibly stole property
While armed with or using or threatening the use of a dangerous instrument or deadly weapon
notes: First-degree robbery is a Class A Felony. Armed criminal action (§ 571.015) may also be charged, adding mandatory minimum.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant unlawfully removed another from the person's place of residence or business
Or unlawfully confined a person for a substantial period
For the purpose of ransom, facilitating a felony, terrorizing, or interfering with government function
notes: First-degree kidnapping is a Class A Felony. Second-degree (§ 565.120) is a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged a building or inhabitable structure
By starting a fire or causing an explosion
Knowing the building was occupied or persons were in the building
notes: First-degree arson involves occupied structures. Second-degree (§ 569.050) involves unoccupied buildings. Third-degree involves property.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant attempted to kill another person
enhancements: Use of a firearm (armed criminal action)
Victim was a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempted murder in Missouri is typically charged as first-degree assault (attempt to kill). Armed criminal action (§ 571.015) may be added.

offense_class: Class D Felony ($750+); Class A Misdemeanor (under $750)
elements: Defendant appropriated property or services of another
Without consent
With the purpose to deprive the owner
enhancements: Stealing from the person (Class D Felony regardless of value)
Third or subsequent stealing (Class D Felony)
notes: Missouri consolidated theft offenses under 'stealing.' Felony threshold is $750. Third stealing offense is a felony regardless of value.

offense_class: Class D Felony ($750–$25,000); Class C Felony ($25,000+)
elements: Defendant appropriated property of another without consent
Value of property was $750 or more
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: Felony stealing threshold is $750 in Missouri.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first/second); Class D Felony (third+)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A); 7 years (third offense Class D)
elements: Defendant appropriated property of another without consent
Value was under $750
With purpose to deprive
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Third misdemeanor stealing is elevated to a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Same as general stealing by value
penalty_max: Same as general stealing by value
fine_max: Same as general stealing by value
elements: Defendant concealed or took possession of retail merchandise
Without paying full consideration
With purpose to deprive the merchant
notes: Shoplifting is charged under the general stealing statute. Merchants may also pursue civil remedies.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly entered unlawfully or knowingly remained unlawfully in a building or inhabitable structure
For the purpose of committing a crime therein
notes: Second-degree burglary covers non-residential structures. First-degree (§ 569.160) involves inhabitable structures at night or with a weapon.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly entered unlawfully or knowingly remained unlawfully in a building or inhabitable structure
For the purpose of committing a crime
While armed with a dangerous instrument or deadly weapon, or while another person was present
notes: First-degree burglary requires entry while armed, at night, or when another person is present. Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony (regardless of value)
elements: Defendant stole a motor vehicle
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: Motor vehicle theft is always a felony regardless of vehicle value.

offense_class: Same class as corresponding stealing offense
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing the property was stolen
notes: Classified at the same level as the corresponding stealing offense.

offense_class: Class D Felony (over $750); Class A Misdemeanor (under $750)
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged property of another
enhancements: Property was a place of worship (Class D Felony regardless of amount)
notes: Missouri uses 'property damage' rather than 'vandalism.' First-degree covers damage to specified structures; second-degree is general.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly entered unlawfully upon real property of another
After being notified not to enter or to leave
notes: First-degree trespass requires notification (signs, verbal, fencing). Second-degree (§ 569.150) is a Class C Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class D Felony (over $750)
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged the property of another
notes: Second-degree property damage is the general criminal mischief charge.

offense_class: Class E Felony (general); Class D Felony (special victim or prior conviction)
elements: Defendant attempted to cause or recklessly caused physical injury to a domestic victim
Domestic victim includes family/household member, spouse, former spouse, or person with whom defendant has a child
enhancements: First-degree domestic assault (§ 565.072, Class B Felony)
notes: Missouri has four degrees of domestic assault. First-degree (serious injury with weapon) is Class B Felony. Fourth-degree (§ 565.076) is Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant attempted to cause or recklessly caused physical injury, pain, or illness to a domestic victim
notes: Fourth-degree is the lowest-level domestic assault. Commonly charged for minor physical altercations.

statute_title: Endangering the Welfare of a Child — First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (general); Class C Felony (substantial risk of death or serious injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly acted in a manner that created a substantial risk to the life, body, or health of a child under 17
enhancements: Substantial risk of death (Class C Felony)
notes: First-degree endangerment is a felony. Second-degree (§ 568.050) is a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class B Felony (general); Class A Felony (if serious injury or death)
elements: Defendant knowingly inflicted cruel and inhuman punishment upon a child under 18
Or knowingly caused serious physical injury to a child
mandatory_minimum: 5 years (Class B, cannot be probated for certain offenses)
enhancements: Serious physical injury or death (Class A Felony)
notes: Child abuse causing death is a Class A Felony. Mandatory reporting by professionals.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class E Felony (second); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: A valid order of protection was in effect
Defendant had notice of the order
Defendant violated a condition of the order
enhancements: Third or subsequent violation (Class D Felony)
notes: First violation is a misdemeanor; second and subsequent violations are felonies. Mandatory arrest for violations.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant purposely and repeatedly harassed or followed another person
And made a credible threat directed at the victim
Causing the victim to reasonably fear for their safety
enhancements: Violation of protective order while stalking
notes: First-degree stalking requires a credible threat plus repeated harassment. Second-degree (§ 565.227) is a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class E Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly communicated a threat to commit a felony
And the threat placed the victim in reasonable fear
notes: First-degree harassment involves felony threats. Second-degree (§ 565.091) is a Class A Misdemeanor for general harassment.

statute_title: Abuse of an Elderly, Disabled, or Vulnerable Person
offense_class: Class D Felony (general); Class B Felony (serious injury)
penalty_max: 7 years (Class D); 15 years (Class B serious injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly caused physical injury, unreasonable confinement, or cruel punishment
To an elderly (60+), disabled, or vulnerable person
notes: Financial exploitation of the elderly is a separate offense under § 570.145. Missouri Adult Protective Services investigates.

offense_class: Class E Felony (general); Class D Felony (certain circumstances)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, carried, or used a weapon in an unlawful manner
Including carrying concealed while intoxicated, carrying into restricted areas, or possessing certain prohibited weapons
enhancements: In a restricted location (school, government building, etc.)
notes: Missouri adopted permitless carry in 2017. Most adults 19+ can carry concealed without a permit. Restrictions remain for prohibited persons and locations.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
offense_class: Class D Felony
penalty_min: 5 years (mandatory minimum under § 571.015 armed criminal action if used in crime)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony under Missouri or federal law
enhancements: Possession during commission of another felony (armed criminal action, 3-year mandatory minimum)
notes: Felon in possession is a Class D Felony. Armed criminal action (§ 571.015) adds mandatory consecutive term if firearm used during felony.

statute_title: Unlawful Use of Weapons — Prohibited Person/Location
offense_class: Class E Felony (prohibited person); Class B Misdemeanor (prohibited location)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed firearm
In a prohibited location or defendant was a prohibited person
notes: Missouri is a constitutional carry state (permitless carry since 2017). Restrictions remain for felons, certain locations, and persons under 19.

offense_class: Class E Felony (general); Class D Felony (at or near person)
elements: Defendant discharged or shot a firearm
At or from a motor vehicle, into a dwelling, or in a manner creating risk of injury
notes: Discharge from a motor vehicle or into a dwelling is a serious felony. Local ordinances may impose additional restrictions.

offense_class: Class D Felony (general); Class B Felony (elderly victim or amount over $25,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly and with intent to deceive or defraud
Used the personal identifying information of another person
To obtain money, credit, goods, services, or other benefit
notes: Enhanced penalties for elderly victims. Restitution ordered.

offense_class: Same as general stealing by value
penalty_max: Same as general stealing by value
fine_max: Same as general stealing by value
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property by virtue of employment or position
Defendant appropriated the property to personal use
Without consent and with purpose to deprive
notes: Embezzlement is charged under the general stealing statute. Value determines classification.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant, with the purpose to defraud, made, completed, altered, or authenticated a writing
So that it purported to be the act of another who did not authorize it
notes: Includes forging checks, identification documents, and other written instruments.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant counterfeited currency, stamps, or government obligations
With purpose to defraud
notes: Federal counterfeiting charges typically apply. State charges may be concurrent.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $750); Class D Felony ($750+)
elements: Defendant issued a check or other instrument for the payment of money
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With purpose to defraud
notes: Same value thresholds as stealing. Restitution typically ordered.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly presented a false or fraudulent insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Missouri Department of Insurance investigates. Restitution and civil penalties may also apply.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Device or Debit Device
offense_class: Class D Felony ($750+); Class A Misdemeanor (under $750)
elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or similar device
Knowing it was stolen, expired, or without authorization
To obtain goods, services, or money
notes: Includes possession of stolen credit cards. Same value thresholds as stealing.

offense_class: Class C Felony (general); Class B Felony (over $500,000)
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction
Knowing the transaction involved proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to promote criminal activity or conceal the source
notes: Federal money laundering charges may also apply.

offense_class: Same as general stealing by value
penalty_max: Same as general stealing by value
fine_max: Same as general stealing by value
elements: Defendant obtained property or services through deception
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: General fraud charged as stealing by deceit under the consolidated stealing statute.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with another person by forcible compulsion
Or the victim was incapacitated or incapable of consent
notes: First-degree rape is a Class A Felony. Second-degree (§ 566.031) is a Class D Felony. Persistent sex offender status carries life imprisonment.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with another person
By forcible compulsion
notes: Missouri uses 'rape' and 'sodomy' in statutes. Forcible compulsion includes physical force, threat, or placing victim in fear of serious injury.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class E Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant exposed genitals
Under circumstances in which the defendant knew the conduct was likely to cause affront or alarm
notes: Progressive penalties for repeat offenders. Third offense becomes a felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class E Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant offered or agreed to engage in sexual conduct with another person
In return for something of value
notes: Progressive penalties. Patronizing a minor for prostitution is a Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony (production); Class D Felony (possession under § 573.037)
penalty_max: 15 years (Class B production); 7 years (Class D possession)
elements: Defendant knowingly used, persuaded, or coerced a minor under 18
To engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions
notes: Possession (§ 573.037) is a Class D Felony. Production and distribution carry mandatory minimums.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
offense_class: Class E Felony (first); Class D Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update information
notes: Missouri Sex Offender Registry. Registration periods vary by tier. Failure to register is itself a felony.

offense_class: Class A Felony (victim under 14); Class C Felony (victim 14-17 with § 566.034)
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with a person under 14 (first degree)
Or with a person under 17 and defendant was 21 or older (second degree)
notes: Age of consent in Missouri is 17. First-degree statutory rape (under 14) is a Class A Felony. Second-degree (under 17, defendant 21+) is a Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant unreasonably and knowingly disturbed or alarmed another person
By fighting, threatening, or violent conduct
Or by loud and unreasonable noise
notes: Missouri uses 'peace disturbance' rather than 'disorderly conduct.' Low-level public order offense.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class E Felony (creating substantial risk of injury)
elements: A law enforcement officer attempted to make a lawful arrest, stop, or detention
Defendant knowingly resisted by using or threatening force
enhancements: Fleeing in a motor vehicle creating substantial risk (Class D Felony)
notes: Resisting by force or threat is a Class A Misdemeanor. Fleeing by motor vehicle creating risk is elevated to felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); higher if aiding felony suspect
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A); 7 years (Class D if aiding felony suspect)
elements: Defendant knowingly harbored, concealed, or aided a person who committed a crime
Or hindered the discovery, apprehension, or prosecution of such person
enhancements: Aiding a felony suspect (Class D Felony)
notes: Covers harboring, concealing, tampering with evidence, and interfering with investigations.

offense_class: Civil or Criminal Contempt
penalty_max: Varies; typically up to 6 months or until compliance
elements: A valid court order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully disobeyed the order
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive. Civil contempt is coercive — defendant can purge by compliance.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant appeared in a public place while intoxicated
Defendant's conduct unreasonably disturbed or alarmed others
notes: Missouri does not have a standalone public intoxication statute. Charged as peace disturbance.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (if underlying misdemeanor); Class D Felony (if underlying felony)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant willfully failed to appear
enhancements: Underlying charge was a felony (Class D Felony)
notes: Bail jumping classification depends on the underlying offense.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (general); Class A Misdemeanor (false fire alarm); Class D Felony (bomb threat)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class B); 1 year (Class A); 7 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant knowingly reported false information to law enforcement
About a crime that did not occur or was materially false
notes: Includes false crime reports, false fire alarms, and bomb threats.

offense_class: Class D Felony (general); Class C Felony (mass violence)
elements: Defendant knowingly communicated a threat to commit a crime of violence
With reckless disregard of the risk of causing terror or evacuation
enhancements: Threat against a school or public building
notes: Making a terrorist threat is a serious felony in Missouri. Includes threats of mass violence.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant, in an official proceeding, made a false statement under oath or affirmation
The statement was material
Defendant knew the statement was false
notes: Includes testimony, depositions, and sworn affidavits.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public servant
With the purpose to influence the public servant's official action
notes: Covers both offering and receiving bribes.

offense_class: Class D Felony (from confinement); Class A Misdemeanor (from custody)
elements: Defendant was in custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape
notes: Escape from confinement is a felony. Escape from custody (arrest, transport) is a misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Class E Felony (torture or killing); Class D Felony (2+ prior convictions)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A); 4 years (Class E); 7 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant intentionally or purposely killed, injured, tortured, or mutilated an animal
enhancements: Two or more prior convictions (Class D Felony)
notes: Missouri strengthened animal cruelty laws. Aggravated animal abuse (§ 578.012(2)) is a Class E Felony.

offense_class: Same as underlying offense
penalty_max: Up to the maximum of the original sentence
elements: Defendant was on probation for a criminal conviction
Defendant violated a condition of probation
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and execute any sentence available. Missouri uses a 120-day shock incarceration program as an alternative.

offense_class: Administrative (revocation)
elements: Defendant was on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Missouri Board of Probation and Parole conducts revocation hearings. Violator may serve remainder of original sentence.

offense_class: Same as principal offense
elements: Defendant aided or encouraged another person in the commission of a crime
With the purpose of promoting the commission of the crime
notes: Accomplice liability. An aider carries the same criminal liability as the principal.

offense_class: One class lower than the target offense
penalty_max: One class lower than the target offense
elements: Defendant, with the purpose of committing a crime, did any act which was a substantial step toward the commission of the crime
notes: Attempt is classified one class lower than the target offense. Attempted murder remains a serious felony.

offense_class: One class lower than the target offense
penalty_max: One class lower than the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator performed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
notes: Conspiracy is classified one class lower than the target offense. An overt act is required.

offense_class: Class B Felony (adult victim); Class A Felony (minor victim)
penalty_max: 15 years (Class B); 30 years or Life (Class A)
elements: Defendant knowingly recruited, enticed, harbored, transported, or obtained another person
Through force, fraud, or coercion
For the purpose of sexual exploitation or forced labor
enhancements: Victim is a minor (Class A Felony)
notes: Missouri enacted comprehensive anti-trafficking legislation. Safe harbor for minor victims.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly restrained another person
Without consent and without lawful authority
notes: False imprisonment is a Class D Felony in Missouri. Lesser included offense of kidnapping.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed an opioid drug
Including heroin, fentanyl, or prescription opioids without valid prescription
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Opioid crisis is a major enforcement priority in Missouri. Drug court diversion programs available.
